advances: An edge-owned scalar charge can be reoptimized as a new same-parity fractional matching. This repairs both affine stress moment cancellations exactly and gives an affine-retention-or-fresh-selector transfer. The repair does not by itself absorb a charge of size \(Q/4000\), or even \(Q/1000\): its first remaining obstruction is the possible equality \(R_C(\beta)=|\beta|\), in which case the fresh load-minimal stress is zero and the original off-chart contacts are not transferred. If the charged matching has genuine affine frustration, the lemma gives a fresh globally dominated endpoint measure of mass at least \(|\beta|-R_C(r)\), with exact rank and support-size screens in the canonical hard branch.

proof:
From (3) and (6),

\[
 d_z(\beta)
 \leq\sum_{e\ni z}\omega_e
 \leq\sum_{e\ni z}r_e
 =d_z(r)
 \leq\frac{a_z}{4}.
\tag{29}
\]

The binomial theorem gives

\[
 \frac1{\gamma_d}
 =\left(1+\frac1d\right)^d
 =\sum_{k=0}^d\binom dk d^{-k}
 \leq\sum_{k=0}^d\frac1{k!}<3,
\tag{30}
\]

so \(\gamma_d>1/3>1/4\). This proves (7). All positive reservoir edges are unordered distinct same-parity pairs, and \(\beta\) is supported on them. Thus \(\beta\) satisfies every other matching hypothesis of accepted fact 6496cb3b0fd44f9d.

By the exact characterization in that accepted fact, \(R_C(\beta)\) is the maximum mass of an affinely half-metronoid-realizable submatching \(\beta'\leq\beta\). Every such \(\beta'\) satisfies

\[
 0\leq\beta'\leq\beta\leq\omega\leq r.
\tag{31}
\]

It is therefore an admissible realizable submatching in the definition of \(R_C(r)=R\). Hence \(|\beta'|\leq R\), and maximizing over \(\beta'\) proves (8).

Apply accepted fact 6496cb3b0fd44f9d to \(\beta\). Its exact dual gives (10), and its gauge-load inequality gives

\[
 B-R_C(\beta)\leq\widehat\Omega\leq B.
\tag{32}
\]

Adding \(R_C(\beta)\) to the first inequality and using (8) proves (11).

The strong endpoint bounds (7) permit the stronger contact measure in accepted fact 6496cb3b0fd44f9d. With the fresh contacts from its support decomposition, that measure is (13), proving its domination and mass. The intrinsic residual bound for that same measure in the accepted fact, multiplied by \(2^n\), is exactly (13c).

Suppose \(\widehat\Omega>0\). Equations (14)-(15) are the objects of accepted fact 6e66cd69e25232b7 under the exact alias map

\[
 q=\beta,\quad
 v=\widehat v,\quad
 \omega_e=\widehat\omega_e,\quad
 r_z=\widehat d_z,\quad
 p_z=\widehat p_z.
\tag{33}
\]

Its simultaneous metronoid, dominated-selector, and residual-selector conclusions give (16)-(18) and the first inequality in (22). Equation (32) gives the second inequality in (22).

Write \(x:=R_C(\beta)\) and \(L:=\widehat L_\beta\). Equations (8), (22), and (32) give

\[
 R+R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)
 \geq x+L(B-x).
\tag{34}
\]

Here \(0\leq x\leq B\). If \(L\geq1\), the right side is at least \(B\); if \(0<L\leq1\), it is at least \(LB\). This proves (23). If \(\widehat r_\beta=0\), an affine map sends each \(z\in E_\beta\) to \(\widehat p_z\). The exact affine case of accepted fact 6e66cd69e25232b7 gives \(G\geq2\widehat\Omega\), and (32) proves (24).

Assume \(B>R\). Equations (8) and (32) give (25). Combining (22) with \(R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)<Q/100\) yields

\[
 2^{n-\widehat\rho_\beta}
 \frac{B-R_C(\beta)}{\widehat r_\beta+1}
 <\frac Q{100}.
\]

Rearranging and using \(R_C(\beta)\leq R\) proves (26). Similarly, (13c), \(D<Q/100\), and (32) give

\[
 2^{n-\widehat\rho_\beta^{\mathrm{edge}}-1}
 \frac{B-R_C(\beta)}
 {\widehat r_\beta^{\mathrm{edge}}+1}
 <\frac Q{100},
\]

which proves (26a).

For each \(z\in E_\beta\), the one-atom submeasure

\[
 \frac{\widehat d_z}{2}
 \delta_{(z,\widehat p_z)}
 \leq\widehat\eta_\beta
\]

is halfspace-dominated by \(\mu_C\). Hence

\[
 h_{\max}(C)\geq\frac{\widehat d_z}{2},
 \qquad
 D\geq2^{n-1}\widehat d_z.
\tag{35}
\]

The bound \(D<Q/100\) gives

\[
 \widehat d_z<\frac{Q}{50\,2^n}
 \qquad(z\in E_\beta).
\tag{36}
\]

Using (16), (25), and (36),

\[
 2\bigl(B-R_C(\beta)\bigr)
 \leq2\widehat\Omega
 =\sum_{z\in E_\beta}\widehat d_z
 <|E_\beta|\frac{Q}{50\,2^n},
\]

and (8) then proves (27).

If one affine map hits every charged \(L_e\), then \(R_C(\beta)=B\) by definition and \(\Delta_C(\beta)=0\) by the primal formula in accepted fact 6496cb3b0fd44f9d. The zero dual field is therefore optimal. Since \(\widehat v\) minimizes the nonnegative gauge load among all optimizers, \(\widehat\Omega=0\). Every \(D_e\) is full-dimensional with the origin in its interior, so \(h_{D_e}\) is a norm; zero total load forces \(\widehat v_e=0\) for every edge. A singleton support is hit by any affine map whose value at its one midpoint belongs to the corresponding nonempty body \(L_e\). This proves (28).

For completeness, (11) gives the following exact threshold audit. If \(B>Q/4000\), then

\[
 R_C(\beta)>\frac Q{8000}
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 \widehat\Omega>\frac Q{8000}.
\tag{37}
\]

If \(B>Q/1000\), then

\[
 R_C(\beta)>\frac Q{2000}
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 \widehat\Omega>\frac Q{2000}.
\tag{38}
\]

The guaranteed quantities in (37) and (38) remain below \(Q/100\). In the fresh-load alternative, the lower bound in (22) is guaranteed to reach \(Q/100\) at the minimal displayed mass only with the additional bounds \(\widehat L_\beta\geq80\), respectively \(\widehat L_\beta\geq20\). In the retention alternative, (28) permits \(\widehat\Omega=0\). Thus the first missing step is a charged-support theorem quantitatively bounding \(R_C(\beta)\) away from \(B\); after that, (22), (26), and (27) give the remaining rank alternatives. This completes the proof.
